{{verse|chapter=4|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō S. Andrewes day.}}And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 5, 1.''}}* vvalking by the sea of Galilee, savv tvvo brethren, Simon vvho is called Peter, & Andrew his brother, casting a nette into the sea (for they vvere fishers) {{verse|chapter=4|verse=19}}† & he sayth to them, Come ye after me, and I vvil make you to be fishers of men. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=20}}† But they incontinent leauing the nettes, folovved him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=21}}† And going forvvard from thence, he savv {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 1, 19. Luc. 5, 10.''}}* other tvvo brethren, Iames of Zebedee & Iohn his brother in a shippe vvith Zebedee their father, repayring their nettes: and he called them. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=22}}† And they furthvvith left their nettes & father and folovved him.⊣

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=23}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent round about all Galilee, teaching in their Synagogs, & preaching the Gospel of the Kingdom: and {{sup|‖}} healing euery maladie and euery infirmitie in the people. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=24}}† And the bruite of him vvent into al Syria, and they presented to him al that vvere il at ease, diuersly taken vvith diseases and torments, and such as vvere possest, and lunatikes, and sicke of the palsey, and he cured them: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=25}}† And much people folovved him from Galilee and Decapolis, and Hierusalem, and from beyond Iordan.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. IIII.}}}}

''1. Desert.''] As Iohn the Baptist, so our Sauiour by going into the desert and there liuing in contemplation euen among brute beasts, and subiect to the assaults of the Diuel for our sinnes, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Eremites.}}geueth a warrant and example to such holy men as haue liued in wildernesse for penance and contemplation, called Eremites.

''2. Fasted fourtie daies.''] Elias and Moyses (saith S. Hierom) by the fast of 40 daies were filled with the familiaritie of God, and our Lord him self in the wildernesse fasted as many, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Lent-fast.}}to leaue vnto vs the solemne daies of fast. (that is, Lent.) ''Hiero. in c. 58 Esa''. S. Augustine also hath the very like wordes ep. 119. And generally al the ancient fathers that by occasion or of purpose speake of the Lent-fast, make it not onely an imitation of our Sauiours fast, but also an Apostolicall tradition, and of necessitie to be kept. ''Contemne not Lent'' (saith S. Ignatius) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Igna. ep. 5.''}}''for it conteineth the imitation of our Lordes conuersation''. And S. Ambrose {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ambr. de Quadrag. ser. 36. 34''.}}saith plainely, that ''it was not ordained by men, but consecrated by God: nor inuented by any earthly cogitation, but commaunded by the heauenly Maiestie''. And againe, that it is sinne not to fast al the Lent. S. Hieroms wordes {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hier. ep. 54 ad Marcel. adu. Montanum''.}}also be most plaine: ''we'' (saith he) ''fast fourtie daies, or, make one Lent in a yere, according to the tradition of the Apostles, in time conuenient''. This time most conuenient is (as S. Augustine saith ep. 119) immediatly before Easter, thereby to communicate with our Sauiours Passion: and (as other writers do adde) thereby to come the better prepared and more worthily, to the great solemnitie of Christes Resurrection: beside many other goodly reasons in the ancient fathers which for breuitie we omitte. See (good Christian Reader) 12 notable sermons of S. Leo the Great ''de Quadragesima'', of Lent: namely Ser. 6 and 9. where he calleth it the Apostles ordinance by the doctrine of the Holy Ghost. See S. Ambrose from the 23 sermon forward: in S. Bernard 7 sermons, and in many other fathers the like. Last of al, note well the saying of S. Augustine, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. Ser. 69. de tēp''.}}who affirmeth that by due obseruation thereof, the wicked be separated from the good, infidels from Christians, Heretikes from faithful Catholikes.<noinclude>{{rh|||''6. It}}</noinclude>
